title: Growing up at Kentucky State: Ellington-style writing and teacher Walter Anderson
summary: He wrote Ellington-influenced arrangements for the campus orchestra and studied music with Walter Anderson, as Milt Hinton later reminded him.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: So I guess, you know, that was quite a chapter. And it has paid off, Pat, you know? If I hadn't gotten that extension in education -- that was about maybe a year or so after my mother died, to go somewhere else, to get the break to go somewhere else. Just don't hang -- don't stay around Chicago, you know, because we were all so tight, you know?
And meeting new people and holding hands, walking around the campus and carrying books and whatever, you know? And it made me grow. I grew quite a bit.
Did you start writing fairly steadily then, or how much?
I did a whole lot of stuff for the orchestra on campus, you know, because they had a piano downstairs
on the ground floor of the dormitory, and I'd go down there and I'd -- let's see, what was some of the stuff? Well, it was all Ellington stuff at that time, because I was deeply influenced, you know.

Uh-huh. I was deeply influenced. By that time it was just about dictated to me what I was going to do without me knowing it. You know? I was going right in that direction, even though I was studying all this -- cramming for exams and sociology and -- but I was going for the music and the second major was music, and I studied with a great teacher, Walter Anderson who is in Washington with the arts -- what's the --

Because Milt Hinton sent me a thick thing, you know, and every time he would mark it in the red -- I was reading through it and he would put a red pencil note and say, 'This is your teacher.' Well, Dr. Anderson, you know? Oh, he taught me counterpoint, and oh, he's a massive musician. And I don't know whether he's still there or not, but he's been there for years. He went from Kentucky State to I think it was either Oberlin or Antioch, in Ohio, you know?
And I didn't realize it -- there's Jack. I didn't realize that he was involved in this until Milt told me. You know?
